utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, good morning. Mr. Siller, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Prosecutor versus Naser Oric, Case Number IT-03-68-T.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Oric, good morning to you. And the usual question, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand? Could someone check the number, whether he has -- Can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, gentlemen, good morning. Yes, I can follow the interpretation, everything the interpreters are interpreting to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution, together with Ms. Patricia Sellers and Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Mr. Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I'm Vasija Vidovic. Together with Mr. John Jones, I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. Together with us are Ms. Jasmina Cosic, legal assistant, and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team, too. So let's go into private session for a while so that we deal with preliminary -- first of all, before we go into private session, do you have any preliminary issues that you yourselves would like to raise? Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones or Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, just one matter. We did receive an email from the Prosecution yesterday with a list of exhibits, description -- a list of exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We replied. Perhaps you've seen our response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen your response. I have a copy of the email that was sent. It wasn't sent to me, obviously, but it was sent to my staff -- I see. Here, I have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just to clarify my understanding, the Prosecution aren't intending to introduce those exhibits today.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. We informed both the Registrar and we informed the Defence of that earlier today, and they expressed absolutely no opposition. We would like to inform the Trial Chamber that those exhibits might be used with other witnesses who come from this village. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. This is something you need to sort amongst yourselves. I would imagine that with the computerised systems that are in place today and which I know that both the Prosecution and Defence adopt here, use, I mean, you can supposedly easily trace a document once you are given the ERN number. I don't know. I mean, correct me if I am wrong. Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what's going to happen, as I explained to you earlier, you are now going to give evidence. The evidence is being given under the solemn declaration that you entered earlier. The procedure is as follows: You will first be asked a set of questions by -- who will be leading, by Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Ms. Patricia Sellers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But Ms. Sellers, who I suppose you have already met. When she finishes with her questions, you will be asked a series of questions by Mr. Jones, who is appearing together with Madam Vidovic for the accused, Naser Oric. Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to say good morning to the witness, first. And for the record, would you please tell the Trial Chamber your name.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Good morning. My name is Dragan Djuric. I was born on the 12th of September 1963 in Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could I ask the witness, how old were you in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And where did you live in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: In my village of Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you tell the Trial Chamber in which municipality Jezestica is located?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The village of Jezestica is in the Bratunac Municipality. It's about 9 to 10 kilometres from Bratunac. And it's in the Kravica local commune. That's the commune that the village is a part of.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you married in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I got married in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did your wife live in the village with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Up to a certain time, she did. But then she was pregnant, and she was going to give birth. She gave birth in September. So she wasn't in the village throughout the whole period.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did your parents live in Jezestica in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were in their house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Trial Chamber, even though we have mentioned it, what is your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: There were only Serbs in our village, so I'm a Serb by ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: About how many people were living in your village in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I didn't know exactly what the number was, but I think there were about 400 to 450 people. There were about a hundred houses in the village, and there were about four or five people in each house. For example, in my house, there were five of us children and our parents. So seven.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And the houses in your village, were they arranged on a hill and by a main highway?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Our village is quite large, so there were houses on the hills and also in the valley along the main road that passes towards Bratunac, Konjevic Polje, Kravica, Zvornik, Sarajevo. So there were houses along that road.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did you live in a house on the hill?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: In addition to your house, were there any other buildings that belonged to you near your house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We had barns and other buildings that were a part of our property. For example, buildings where we held our grain, our agricultural machinery. Yes, we did have some additional buildings, the old house and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you have any farm animals near your house on the hill?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We had cows. They were out in the field. Naturally, these were all a part of village life. We had goats. We had cows. Chickens. Domestic animals that any householder would have, any person who owned land for his own needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992, let's say between March and June of that year, do you recall if there were any tensions in your village or the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't really remember if there were any tensions in that particular period.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did any people that lived in your village or the surrounding villages, did any decide to leave because of any tensions that they might have felt?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Next to our village, there were other hamlets, for example Bukova Glava and Dubova, these two villages. And I know that people from there had to leave their villages. They came to our village, as well. Some of them if they had family or relatives in our village came to ask for shelter there, or they continued farther away to go and stay with close friends or families. But they did have to leave their own homes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: The people that you're speaking about who left their homes and came through your village, would you please tell me whether they were Bosnian Serbs or Bosnian Muslims.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They were Bosnian Serbs from those two villages, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did there come a moment in the spring of 1992 when your village formed a village guard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: People had left their homes. They came, and they were telling us about what the situation was, and people had to be careful that the same thing, perhaps, would happen to us and that one day we would have to leave our homes just as they had to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did you form a village guard in your village, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I did not, but probably there was some kind of guard.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether this village guard wore uniforms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Some people had uniforms from the reserves, and others did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether the village guard was armed? Did they carry weapons or rifles?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They did. Some had hunting rifles, some had pistols. So... Yes, they did have some weapons. Some people did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: In August of 1992, was the village of Jezestica attacked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: In August, on the 8th of August, the village of Jezestica was attacked. And --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Was the 8th of August -- pardon me. Was the 8th of August a holiday?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The 8th of August was some kind of a holiday for us. It was marked in red in our calendar. It was some kind of holiday, for us, Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Because it was a holiday, did people stay home, or did people go to work on that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, you know how it is, perhaps out -- in the different companies, the businesses were not working. But those who were cultivating the land did continue to work. Those people who were farther away from the centre of the village were able to cultivate their land, and those who were closer to the woods were not really able to do that. So it depended from person to person; some people did work on their land and others did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: You testified that the village was attacked on that day. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber at what time during the day the village was attacked.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The village was attacked at about 11.30 that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Who attacked the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It was attacked by Muslims, our neighbours from the neighbouring villages that bordered on our village.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were the Muslims from these neighbouring villages, were they wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I did see some people in uniforms. They were wearing some kind of uniform, from what I could see.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And the people who attacked, were they men or were they women?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: You mean the people who were attacked? I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: The people who were attacking your village. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Those who were attacking, they were men. They were armed men who were shooting in our village. They were shooting at the houses in the village. Our house was also hit. A shell fell near the house. There was the old house and the new house, and the electricity cable connected the old house and the new house. And this was hit by some kind of projectile, and it hit the cable. It did not hit the house directly. And it exploded.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: What direction were the uniformed men coming from as they attacked your village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: There are woods around our village, and they could come in from different directions to get into our village. They could have come from Jaglici, from their villages. But since our village is divided in two parts, they came from different directions, from Jaglici, Cizmici, and they attacked Djermani, Jezestica, Trisici, Rankovici, all these hamlets belonging to Jezestica. And there was also one hamlet that was on the other side. They were these hamlets that were on the hills all belonging to the village of Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, where were you standing when you first saw this group of armed men coming into your village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We were near our house. We heard shooting, and we then could see people approaching the houses from several sides, because the position of our village is such that it's on hilly terrain. So they were coming from several directions into the village and coming to the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you in your house on the hill at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was there then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And then did you ever leave your house during the attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I had to leave the house. We fled from that village. We went through the village and fled from the village and hid behind the hill where there was less danger. So whoever managed to get away from the village did. And of course, there are more people living in the valley than up on the hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: As you were fleeing at that point, did you hear the attackers say anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, we did. They were clamouring, they were shouting, they were cursing our Serbs mothers. They were saying "Go to Serbia."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you see these attackers, the uniformed men, did you see them doing anything as you were fleeing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They were about 300 metres away. So we had to flee. We had to run away. As they entered the village, we saw that houses were on fire Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and that they were shooting in the villages. People who were in the village had to run for their lives, as you would say. And they were trying to get as far away as possible. Whoever was in the village did not survive.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you see the village guard fighting the soldiers in the camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: From where I was, I could not see that. From where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, how long did the attack last?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: How long? Well, a while. Perhaps two hours, an hour and a half. The houses were on fire. They were burning. The people who managed to get out did, and those who stayed behind were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, you said you were fleeing. Did you flee from the hills to the bottom part of Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes. We were fleeing from our houses. We were going away from the village and from the woods. We were going to the lower part of the village of Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you hear shooting while you were fleeing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Of course we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you hear any grenades or other types of artillery coming from the uniformed soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Some projectiles hit my house, as I told you. Now, whether these were handheld launchers or mortars or whatever, I'm not very knowledgeable about these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you have a chance --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Detonations could be heard, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Excuse me. Did you have a chance after the attack to speak to two women from the village, one named Stanica Djuric, and the other name Perka Djuric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: After the attack, yes. They had also sought shelter from the village somewhere in the woods. So they came to us from the village down there in the valley, in the fields, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I anticipate we're probably coming for the first time in this trial to an issue of hearsay. I know there's no hearsay rule here. Unless it would be useful for our part to have some guidance as to how this will be approached. Because if you say hearsay evidence will be given when we don't know on what basis the declarants got their information from, then it could be extremely unreliable. And that would be something we would object to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Basically, Mr. Jones, you clear this away from your mind. I thought I had made it clear when we issued the guidelines that the rule here is the inverse of what you are used to. The rule here is to admit hearsay evidence, rather than to be watchful and on guard against hearsay evidence. The rule is to admit hearsay evidence. These are cases that without hearsay evidence you couldn't possibly go along. But then at the end, it's the criteria that it will use in assessing the probative value that we will give to each and every piece of hearsay evidence. Hearsay evidence is going to be accepted throughout the entire trial. But then what weight we give it, we will decide at the very end.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm obviously well aware of that. As you'll note, I said I know there's no hearsay rule here. I'm the last person who is going to come here and insist on following some national procedure. The reason I mention it is because I was wondering whether it would be necessary for my learned friend to establish some foundation for the basis on which the declarants made their statements or whether that's something we have to do in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First of all, I think it has got more to do with the cross-examination. And in an adversarial system, you will understand that we will interfere as little as possible. The Prosecution knows, and you know, that you can bring forward hearsay evidence and that ultimately the weight that we might give to that hearsay evidence may be less than we would give to direct evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it's a question of how you play your cards at the end of the day, you know. I mean -- but we are not going to interfere. Definitely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just to be clear on that from the outset.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, sorry for the interruption, Ms. Sellers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm grateful, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'll go back to my last question. I wanted to ask you: After the attack, did you have a chance to speak to two women from the village, Stanica Djuric and Perka Djuric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, after the attack, we did talk. They said that they sought shelter in a small thicket. They got all of this village, this hamlet of Djermani, the village of Trisici, for instance. And that's where they were in the woods. They went through the woods. These were our neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did these two women tell you what they saw during the attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, they saw people running around torching houses, shooting. They saw better than we did. We were closer to the houses, so we had to flee further away. Our houses were on the outskirts of the village. So they would be the first to be attacked.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, the people that they saw torching the houses, were these people wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They were probably, yes, yes, wearing uniforms. Some did have uniforms; others did not. That's what the women said at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And were these the same people that were carrying guns that you described earlier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, it all depended on who was where and who could see which people from where, if you can follow this. There are many paths leading to the village and roads leading to the village. And now, it depends. Not everybody took the same paths and the same roads.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Let me rephrase it. Witness, are you saying that it was attackers who were torching the houses? Is that who you were referring to, or that the women were referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they were torching the houses, these attackers who were there, the Muslims. They were torching our houses, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: After the attack, did you go back up to your house on the hill?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: After the attack, perhaps two or three hours later, we went up to see what had happened. We saw that the entire village was in smoke. We went back to see what had happened and whether there was anything left, whether anything was left of the house, whether the house was in the same condition that I had left it in or whether it was burned down. It had been burning, the top floor. But it was only the cellar that did not burn. We had this kitchen in the cellar, and we slept upstairs. That's where the rooms were and the bathroom and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So did the top floor of your house suffer complete fire damage?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, the roof had caught fire. I'm talking about my house now. My house was made of bricks. And also, there were wooden structures. There were wooden beams, and everything was on fire. However, the cellar could not burn because there was a stone wall. It wasn't wooden beams. And that's why this did not catch fire, but of course the rest had burned down during the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Can you describe the condition your barn was in after you went back up after the attack.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Our barn, I had to walk by it before I came to the house. The barn was on fire. It had burned down to the concrete blocks that were used for building the walls. So it was still smouldering, and there was still smoke there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And could you find your farm animals after the attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. The cow had been in the field, so it was not in the barn in the first place. So it was tied in the field, but it wasn't there. The goats weren't there either. The pigs were let out. Before that, they were not corralled in any way. They could walk around the farm. The pigs would roam about anyway. There were two pigs as we arrived. And then there was corn near our house. So then the other pigs had been in the cornfield, and then they came to the house later. But the cows, we couldn't see the cows. We couldn't find the cows, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you see the other houses that were your neighbours' houses on the hills after the attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We had to pass by some houses, and these houses were burning, too. Most of the houses were burning. Some had burned down completely; others had not burned down completely but they were burning. In Trisici, a hamlet near us, there was a house there. It hadn't burned down. The new house hadn't been burned probably because it wasn't completed yet. But the old house next to it had burned down. This is Trisic -- the Trisic family. Trisic Slavoljub was the head of that household. He died before the war so his wife and his children were the owners of that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you able after the attack to return and live in your house immediately after?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We couldn't. Everything was burned down, destroyed. It's not only me. Nobody could go back to the village, to the hill, because we had no place to live.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So where did the people who used to live on the hill in your village, where did they go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Some people went away; others stayed. Some people had relatives down in the valley, a brother, an uncle, whatever. Other people went to Bratunac, to Serbia, wherever, because they couldn't go on living in burned houses and destroyed houses. So some people went to other places, and other people stayed behind if they had someone who could put them up in the village. Others had family in Serbia or in Bratunac or wherever, so then they left the village. Quite a few people did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Witness, to your knowledge, did the Army of the Republika Srpska fight against those uniformed, armed -- what you described as Muslims on that day of August 8th in your village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you: Perhaps they did fight somewhere, but then in other places they didn't. All of this happened suddenly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you see any members of the Republika Srpska Army in your village that day during the attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Afterwards, some soldiers came. After the village had burned down, some soldiers came. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you see during the attack any soldiers from Republika Srpska Army fighting the uniformed men?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Some soldiers came and went up to the village, towards the burned village, the village that had burned down. They went up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And was this after the attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: After the attack, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to describe to the Trial Chamber what life was like in the village after the attack up until January of 1993, if you could.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Life was terrible in that village. That's the only thing a person can say. Our neighbours and I, we couldn't do anything with the crops we had planted up on the hills. People had left the villages. There was some kind of fear among the people, among the villagers. The time will come when we will all have to leave, including the people who lived in the valley. I lived in my wife's house in the valley later on. Some people thought that the time would come when everybody from the village would have to leave their property, their houses, the property that they were building up for centuries and that they worked so hard for.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did there come a time when the village was attacked again?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: A time did come, yes. This was later, a few months later, on the 7th of January. What remained of our village, that is, that flat area in the valley, it was attacked on the 7th of January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And the 7th of January, is that a holiday?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The 7th of January is a holiday for us, the Christian Orthodox Serbs. It's Christmas. All the Serb people celebrate Christmas on the 7th of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And at what time on Christmas Day was your village attacked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: At what time? Early in the morning, around 5.30 or 6.00. Our village was attacked from several different directions. The villages in the hills were not attacked any more because they burned down. So they got closer to our village. So Mandici, the neighbouring village, Siljkovici, many villages in the Kravica area. There was shooting. Shooting started from all sides. They were shooting at our village and the other villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Trial Chamber who was shooting at your village. Who attacked your village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Our village was attacked probably by the same people. These Muslims, our neighbours, these soldiers. They attacked our village, what had remained of our village and these other villages around it from the commune of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: What were the Muslim soldiers wearing on that day when they attacked the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: These soldiers who I could see - and it was hard to see them because there was a lot of snow there - they had some kind of uniforms on, white uniforms, so it was hard to see them. It's hard to see a white uniform in the snow. You cannot tell it apart from the snow. There was a lot of snow then, perhaps 50 or 65 centimetres of snow. That's how deep or how high, whatever, the snow was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So did the white uniforms of the soldiers act as a type of camouflage because of the snowy conditions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Most probably so, so that it would be difficult to see them, a white uniform, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could I ask you now, where were you when this attack began on the 7th of January?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We were near our house down there in the village. Shooting started from different directions. So people are bound to panic in a situation like that, where to go, where to flee. The people who were there set out towards Kravica, towards the main road, the asphalt road. The houses that were closer to them that were the first to be attacked, they were already on fire. You could see the smoke coming from those houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did you come out of your house and see those houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We had to go out. We could not wait. So the houses could be seen, yes. My house, or rather, my wife's house had burned down on the 8th of August, so this is where I was. My wife has no brothers. She did have a sister, but her sister did not live there. So it was as if it were my house, too. We lived there together and we maintained the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When you left your house, did you go toward the main road?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We went towards the main road, the asphalt road to Kravica, because our only way out was to go to Kravica because there were shooting coming from neighbouring villages. So we went towards Kravica. Jezestica was attacked, Mandici, the neighbouring village. Also Siljkovici. These were the places where we heard shooting coming from, and we noticed what was happening in those villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And what was happening in those villages that you saw?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We heard gunfire, and we saw people torching houses in my village. I couldn't see it in Siljkovici or Mandici. I couldn't see the people. I could see the smoke. But there is a distance involved. It's a few kilometres away. But in my village, I could see the people who were shooting from different directions. Also, I could see houses being set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And was it the same people who attacked your village who set the houses on fire in your village? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They were Muslims, but I don't know whether they were the same ones that did it the first time. I couldn't recognise any of them. People who were closer to them could recognise them. But it's not that somebody stayed behind in their house. Whoever stayed behind in their own houses was killed or burned in the house or killed in front of the house. Anybody who could find out more or see more. These people are considered to be as missing, but I haven't seen any of these people until the present day, and no one from our neighbourhood could find anything out about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: The people you're referring to as missing, are they villagers from your village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: From our village, yes, yes. They didn't find them. They didn't bury them. Now, whether animals devoured them and that's why their bodies couldn't be found or whether they were taken away somewhere, that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And the people who were setting fire to the houses, were they the men in the white uniforms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, you know what? They were getting close to houses, entering houses, shooting at houses. But we just saw smoke. We did not see whether they were setting the houses on fire. We could not see them setting fire to the houses. But we saw smoke coming from the roofs and from the windows, and that meant that the houses were on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And this is after they walked into the houses or went into the houses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We saw them come to the houses, approach the houses, these houses that were further away. So smoke came out of the houses through the windows or the roofs. So we realised that the houses were burning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was about to say. We'll be finished, but there will be another segment so I suggest we take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's a good idea, Ms. Sellers. So what we will do is we will have a 25-minute break. In the meantime, Mr. Jones, please be prepared to start your cross-examination during the next session.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed, Ms. Sellers, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Witness, I have just a couple more questions. I believe you testified that you were fleeing on the main road toward Kravica after the second attack on Jezestica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We were moving towards Kravica along the main road. And there's a canal and a small river along this road, so some people were going along the road. Some were taking the canal. Some were walking in the little river. But that was the road that we took.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Who were the people who were fleeing with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: These were people from my village, from the village. My neighbours from the village. One young man, I don't know whether he was from Kravica or from somewhere else, but he was along with me at that point in time. I don't know whether he was from Kravica or from some other village. But he joined me, and we reached Kravica together.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Did there come a time when you were going up the road that you were wounded or injured?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: When I made it to the road, I was not. When we were leaving the village, at that point, from my house, then maybe some six or seven hundred metres away from my house, that's where I was wounded. I was wounded near a house. I was trying to shelter myself there and to reach the river so that I could take the river towards Kravica. But I was injured there. I was wounded there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber where on your body you were wounded.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I was wounded in the neck near the spine.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And do you know who could have inflicted the wound? I mean not necessarily the name of the person, but the type of the person.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know the name of the person. All I know is that across the street, across from the asphalt road, the neighbours from our -- from the neighbouring Muslim village were firing at us some 30 to 50 metres away from where I was -- from behind a house. They were shooting at us. I was wounded. I fell down. And the man who was walking in front of me noticed that, so he helped me. So we managed to reach this small river that goes from my village to Kravica, and we took -- we walked in this small river all the way from the village to Kravica, to the local commune of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether the people who were shooting at you were wearing the white camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The people who were shooting at us were wearing uniforms. They were the ones who were shooting at us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: After you reached Kravica, did you have to go to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went to the hospital. I was in the hospital in Zvornik for treatment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And after you left the hospital, were you able to return to your village to live?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We were not able to return to the village because it was burned, destroyed, plundered. It was not possible to go back because the houses had burned down. After that, my wife came to visit me in the hospital. And when I left the hospital, I went to see my wife and one child in Sabac. We stayed with my sister. Then we went to Belgrade to stay with my uncle. So I was moving from one relative to another. I spent a couple of months here, a couple of months with my family. We kept going round to different relatives.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: In October of 1993, were you drafted into the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: In October or thereabouts, I think I came back from there. I came to visit my parents, and we were then picked up by the police and mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Witness, I just have one final question I would like to ask, and that is: Were you ever paid or given money for the damage to your property or for the loss of your livestock, the animals, or any of your equipment due to the attack on either the 7 -- the 8th of August 1992 or the 8th of January -- I'm sorry, the 7th of January 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: There was no compensation as far as my village is concerned, the upper part of the village. We didn't receive any aid, any compensation for damages or anything like that. But the place where I'm living now, I did receive a donation for a house. My wife, her father, she doesn't have any sisters or brothers, we are actually supporting her father. So we received assistance. We received a donation in order to build a house where we are living today. However, we didn't receive any compensation. We just received a -- some assistance in order to build a house. We received the material.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Sellers. You are now going to be cross-examined by Mr. Jones, who is one of the lawyers appearing for Mr. Oric. It is my responsibility -- I think your client has got something for you. It is my responsibility to draw your attention to something which we consider very important, namely that although you have been summoned here to give evidence by the Prosecution, by the Office of the Prosecution, you are testifying under the solemn obligation to say the truth -- to speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. So you have a responsibility also not to make any distinction between the Prosecution and the Defence. Your obligation, your duty under the solemn declaration that you have taken is to answer the questions that the Defence will now put to you in the same way and with the same truthfulness and completeness, fullness, that you have answered the questions of the Prosecution. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Mr. Jones, you may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, you mentioned this morning that you have given two statements in the past, one in Bratunac and one in Milici. Were those both to the Office the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I'm very sorry to interrupt. But I believe that was testimony that was held in private session, and that is not part of the record. I would just ask that that possibly be rephrased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think you are right, Ms. Sellers. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I can certainly do that. It was only to avoid confusing the witness by referring to private session or closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can ask the same question that was asked in private session this morning in any case. There's nothing stopping you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, it is right that you have given two statements in the past, one in Bratunac and one in Milici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that as being so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And were those both given to the Office of the Prosecutor, or did you give a statement also to the Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I did not give any statements to the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, it's right, isn't it, that your father's name is Cedo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is that a nickname or is that his full name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: That's his full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Or did you when you were younger?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that you have a brother, Savo, a couple of years younger than you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you've lived in Jezestica all your life?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You told us that Jezestica is part of the local community of Kravica, which is in the Municipality of Bratunac. So I want to ask you a question about the Kravica community. And I'm going to mention some hamlets, and you can say yes or no whether they're in the Kravica community.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, again, sorry to interrupt you. Why don't we make available for ourselves and for everyone, including members of the public, a map of the area so that we can understand better.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. It was something I was hoping would be produced in examination-in-chief. I have a rough photocopy which could be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before we put it on the ELMO, could you hand it over to the Prosecution for verification that they agree with it. Otherwise, if not, perhaps we can get an official map. Do you have any objections, Ms. Sellers, if we use that map?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's put that map on the ELMO, please. Now, we will need -- the technician's on notice already -- we will need to zoom in and out as we go along. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. You'll see I've highlighted certain towns and areas on that map.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Can you, Mr. Djuric, first of all, find Kravica on the map.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we zoom in. For the record, the Trial Chamber notices that the accused [sic] has pointed to a spot on the map, which upon being zoomed in shows the name "Kravica."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just as a matter of orientation, and you're free to disagree with me, Mr. Djuric, if I get this wrong, that you have the Drina towards the north, curving around to the side, with Bratunac on the bottom right-hand corner of our screen. If you could point to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, it states here on the map, Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The road you've referred to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Jones. For the record the Trial Chamber notices that the accused [sic] has pointed to a spot on the map --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. This is a Prosecution witness, not the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry. The witness has pointed to a spot on the map which upon being zoomed shows the name Bratunac. Thank you Ms. Sellers for pointing that out. I mixed Mr. Jones with Mr. Nichols and the witness with the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If you could, Mr. Djuric, could you just trace the course of the road from Bratunac which goes to Konjevic Polje, which you've referred to as the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That passes through Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, to a part, it -- Jezestica goes all the way to Gajici. So the road goes from Bratunac. Is that -- that's -- is that the road that goes there? Jezestica reaches that part near Kajici, on this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think we can all see Jezestica there. Is that right? If you could point to it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's that part there where it says Jezestica, Jazbine. All of that belongs to Jezestica. These are the hamlets of Jazbine. Jezestica, Rankovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jezestica. Djermani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the Trial Chamber notices that the witness has pointed out the asphalt road indicated to him as well as to one spot on the map which upon being zoomed shows the name of Jezestica, also the village of Djermani.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Perhaps we can just leave the map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's a good idea, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But the witness needn't refer to it any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You can put down the pointer. Now I'm just going to mention the names of some hamlets and you can confirm yes or no whether they're in the Kravica community, if that's clear. First of all, obviously, Jezestica and Kravica. I won't mention those, but they're obviously in that community. I'm waiting for the translation. Okay, let's start. Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Villages after that? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I'll mention names of hamlets, and then you just say yes or no if it's in the Kravica community. Okay?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know each and every hamlet. But in my own village, I know every hamlet. However, as far as the neighbouring villages are concerned, I don't know. There are many of them in Kravica. But there are some Serb villages there, so...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll just mention them, and you say yes, no, or I don't know. Kravica. Obviously in its own community. Donji Bacici.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Brezanci.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Brezanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Brezanci, sorry.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Brezanci. I know that children from there went to the Kravica school, so that belongs to the Kravica local community. I don't know. I know that the whole village is called Lipenovici, but I'm not sure about the hamlets. There are some other hamlets, Ratinci [phoen] and so on. I don't know whether that is part of the Kravica or the Lipinci local community. I don't know. But the children went to the school there, the same elementary school that I attended, the one that has the eight-year elementary school in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Dolovi.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Dolovi, yes, that is also near Brezanci. It is all part of the Lipenovici village. I don't know if all of them are in the Kravica local community. The children did go to the Kravica school. So I don't know. I'm not sure. I'm not able to tell you how -- what each village borders on and which local community it belongs to.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We don't need that much detail. It's really simple if you can say whether or not it's in the rough area of Kravica. If one seems to be way outside, then you can let me know. Lazarici is the next one.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Lazarici, this is a village near Siljkovici. It's a hamlet. The hamlet of Lazarici and the village of Siljkovici. They belong to the Kravica local community, Lazarici. This is a hamlet, part of the Siljkovici village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You can simply say yes or no for each of these places. There's no need to elaborate each time. Yes or no, whether they're in the Kravica community. Marici.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Donji Bacici.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Jezero, Kravica Jezero.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: There are some hamlets called Jezero. I don't know which one you exactly mean. Perhaps the one that's part of Bacici. Well, I didn't go to many of those villages. I had nothing to do there, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what is a part of each of those villages. I know that our village does belong to that local community, but as far as other villages are concerned, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Ocenovici.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Ocenovici, yes. Yes, they should be a part of the community, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I also know that the children attended the same elementary school that I did, so probably yes, that is a part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Popovici.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, also I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Vrane.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And Opravdici.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Those are all part of the Kravica local community as far as you know, the towns I've mentioned, villages I've mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know whether we should proceed along these lines any further. Because these are things that you could easily agree amongst yourselves. If you make out a list of all the villages, hamlets or whatever, that you believe formed part of this community or municipality or call it whatever you like, you can submit it to the Prosecution, they can agree with it; and if there is one or two or more hamlets they don't agree upon, you can lead questions on those. But otherwise, this is going to go on and on and on when we can deal with it in a different matter. That's why we have the system of agreeing on facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, it won't go on and on and on. The reason why I'm posing this question is because it's relevant to this witness's knowledge whether those villages were part of the local community, because it's relevant to other answers he has given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Basically how much weight do you think the Trial Chamber is going to give to the testimony of this witness who may think he knows?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour will see when I get to that part of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can easily get another witness who will tell you exactly the opposite, if he happens to know more or less than this witness. But these things can be quickly established in a much more formal way. Anyway, finish this exercise as quickly as you can and proceed to the more substantial part of your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, I was about to ask you the hamlets of Jezestica, which is obviously your town. Djermani is where you were living. Is Kajici part of your hamlet?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: To a part, yes, we do go up to Kajici. Kajici is also in the same local community, in the Kravica local commune. We pass through Kajici. On the map, you can see the village of Kajici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And now, Magasici, is that a Serb village? Was it before the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, Magasici is a neighbouring village, next to Jezestica. It was a mixed village, both peoples lived there as far as I know. I didn't really go to Magasici all that much. I didn't have any relatives or friends there. So I wasn't really there much, and I don't know too much about it. All I know is that when we went to school, I remember that both ethnic groups also went there from Magasici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned neighbouring Muslim villages where you say the attacks came from. I think you said, correct me if I'm wrong, that that's Jaglici and Cizmici. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Jaglici is behind our village, behind Jezestica. On one side of Jaglici, and then on the other side there is Bukova Glava, Jaglici. I don't know the names of all of these villages. I don't know the order that they go in. I know about Jaglici because those people, we did not go to school with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting you, but His Honour has made clear that we want to make rapid progress if we can. If you keep your answers short and try to answer in simple terms my questions. Jaglici and Cizmici are in Bratunac Municipality. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I'm not sure whether some of them belonged to the Srebrenica commune. I know that our village belongs to the Bratunac Municipality, but as far as the neighbouring villages that are further along, I'm not sure if they're part of the Bratunac Municipality or not. That's not something that I am aware of. I don't know exactly to which municipality they belong.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I want to go back to Magasici briefly. You said that was a mixed village before the war. During the war, though, it was no longer a mixed village, was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, would you say that the Muslims in Magasici remained there throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: As far as I heard, I think that they did not, but I'm not sure. I didn't really go to Magasici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But they did not -- the Muslims in Magasici did not remain in Magasici during the war. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I think that they did not. They were partially -- I know that the Serbian village of Magasici was burned down. I know that a colleague of mine who was doing the same work as I was, that he was killed. That's as far as Magasici is concerned. I think he was doing construction work as well. We worked together.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know where the Muslims from Magasici went and what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Let me ask you about Glogova. If you could point to Glogova on the map with the pointer. Perhaps it's not necessary. I think we can see it. It's right in the centre of the screen. Stop there, please. Right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the witness points to a spot on the map which upon being zoomed shows the name Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, that's very near you, isn't it, very near Jezestica? You don't have to go on the map. You can tell us on the basis of your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Glogova, I mean, one passes through Glogova when going from Jezestica. It's not too far away, only a few kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So you must know it very well and you must have passed by practically every day of your life.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I still pass through it when I'm there, so yes, I do. I mean -- I don't know what you mean, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You simply have to answer the questions, and we'll take it from there. Glogova was a Muslim village before May 1992, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It was. I know that there are some Serb houses there, too. I don't know whether they belonged to Glogova or Avdagina Njiva. But I know that there were some Serbs living there in Glogova, I think. Now, did they come from Magasici in part? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that there were about 2.000 Muslims living in the Glogova area before the war, a large community?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know how many people lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... estimate.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You estimate there are four to five hundred people in Jezestica. If you know, how many people are in Glogova, if you can help us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: How can I know how many there were when --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues].... Now, Bratunac Municipality as a whole, was it not mostly Muslims before the war, 21.500 Muslims, 11.500 Serbs. Does that sound right to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Witness, if you know the answer, answer it. Give an answer. If you know, please go ahead. If you don't know, just say "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly. I never did. It's not that I am some kind of authority to keep records of this kind and to write how many people live where. There's no way I can know this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Of course not. The reason I'm asking this is because the questions which I'll be asking you are designed to discover what happened to the Muslims in Bratunac Municipality during this period. So you lived in Bratunac Municipality throughout the war. You must be aware that it was taken over by the Serbs in April 1992. Is that something you're aware of or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It is correct that I lived in Bratunac. My house burned down, and I know that they let us stay wherever it was possible to stay, where there was accommodation available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's not the question that was put to you. Mr. Jones, could you repeat the question again. It's not because you didn't make yourself clear, but it's because the witness has avoided answering it. Could you please put the question again. And Witness, please, try to answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The question is are you aware that April 1992, the municipality which you live in, Bratunac, was taken over by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, I mean, I'm not very knowledgeable about these things. I wasn't there. I had had an operation. I was in Serbia. You see what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... I don't know. Have you heard of the Serbian Democratic Party, the SDS?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I have heard of it. Of course I've heard of it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Have you heard of Miroslav Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He was born in Magasici and was practically a neighbour of yours. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, I heard that he had been born there, but I have never been to Magasici, and I never spoke to the person or met him. I don't know him. He belongs to an older generation. I know the people who went to school with me, people of that age group.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, I would appreciate it if you would try to keep your answers shorter. We don't have so much time. A yes or a no will suffice to the questions I'm about to ask you. Are you aware that Deronjic was the president of the Serb Crisis Staff in your municipality in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know about all these authorities that kept changing. I don't know who was where at which point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So you didn't know anything really of what was happening politically in your municipality during the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I was not involved in any such thing, and I don't know what was going on. I've never belonged to any party. I don't know anything about such matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are you aware that there was an order to disarm Muslims in Bratunac Municipality, but at the same time the Serbs were armed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We have a Defence exhibit. It was -- it's going to be D3, but I've skipped the first two exhibits. Copies have been distributed. If that could be put on the ELMO and see if it jogs the witness's memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Distributed to whom? I don't recall having seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: To the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We would just like to state also that we were unaware there were going to be exhibits used during the Defence part, which certainly they have a right to do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: -- but I don't know whether the procedure we're setting up is to inform the other party --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you don't have that procedure in place, we will impose it. Because you can't have a system where I expect -- or we expect -- the Trial Chamber expects you to disclose or to make -- indicate to the Defence the documents you're going to make use of the day after and the day after possibly, while the Defence hasn't got that responsibility. So for the future, if you intend to make use of documents during your cross-examination, you're expected to inform the Prosecution and the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Trial Chamber at least the day before or when you have made up your mind that you would be making use of those documents. Because just as you need time to check on the documents that the Prosecution will be making use of, the Prosecution also has got that right. So it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm making these decisions as I go along. As you'll see, this is D3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay, I appreciate, because I have done cross-examinations in my life as well. And it may well be that documents become necessary to produce as you go along. But there are also documents which you certainly plan beforehand to make use of, such as this document. Because this is not a question which has just fallen from heaven. This is a question that was planned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If the witness had said yes, that is what happened, then there would be no need for the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but in cross-examination you also anticipate that he may say no. So please be as transparent as possible with each other. I expect the Prosecution to do what they did for the purpose of today's sitting, giving us a list of documents they possibly will use, and I expect the Defence to do the same. There will be exceptions, obviously. The need will rise from time to time to resort to a document that was unthought of, which was not planned to bring forward, but that should be the exception and not the rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Your Honour. At the same time, you're obviously aware that the disclosure obligations are not the same on each party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is not disclosure. This is not disclosure. This is -- as I said, the trial system nowadays is not taking the other party or the other side by surprise. I mean, it's no longer the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My intention wasn't to take anyone by surprise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sure of that. I'm sure that this is something that perhaps we did not make ourselves clear on from the very beginning. But we are definitely making ourselves clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm going to leave that exhibit aside for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, you can use it, Mr. Jones. I mean, there's no problem with using it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic was indicted, as you may or may not be aware, by this Tribunal for crimes against humanity committed in Glogova, Bratunac. And when he was interviewed by the Prosecution, he said certain things which I'm going to put to you and ask you questions about. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's start with the first question, because you have already asked him a question and you're moving to the second. Are you aware, sir, that Miroslav Deronjic stood -- was indicted before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know about that. I am aware of that. But I'm not that familiar with it. I don't follow this. It's not that I follow the news or -- I mean, I don't know how and in which way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware that he pleaded guilty and was eventually sentenced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, I don't really keep abreast of all these events. I don't read the newspapers, and I don't watch television. I have such a lot of my own work that I don't really follow politics, and I'm not really that well informed. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Back to you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm going to put certain things which he said to you for your comment. The first is he said, speaking of how the SDS prepared for war by arming Serbs and forming units in the field, he said: "So in Bratunac, we had three small Serb units, upstream from the Drina and downstream in Kravica. So what we tried to do was to form units made up of local people. We tried to form some form of commands. We called them detachments." Now, stopping there, detachments, I suppose, would be ceta in Serbian. Is that right? Well, you don't have to confirm that. My question is --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I know that I was at my home in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So is it your evidence that you were not in one of these detachments before I think --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I was not, no. No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are you sure about that? Are you sure about that? You weren't in a detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I was not, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll get back to that. He went on to say, Mr. Deronjic, "Real war operations began in Srebrenica after the 17th of April, and we in the SDS leadership took over power in Bratunac. I'm not sure exactly when this was, but I think it was the end of April. I think that was correct. And then we formed a municipal crisis staff." Now, stopping there, is it your evidence that you're not aware a crisis staff was formed and there was a takeover of power in Bratunac? You can answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you travel to Bratunac during this period, to the town of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All the time you were in your village, tucked away, unaware of what was going on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Another thing he said "after the 20th of April" - that's 1992 - "a military unit of the JNA arrived in Bratunac led by Mr. Reljic who was a captain by rank." So stopping there, according to that, the JNA arrived in Bratunac in April; that's the federal Yugoslav army. You're saying that you didn't see tanks, transporters, artillery being moved along the road to Bratunac. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I myself was not in Bratunac. Some vehicles were travelling along the roads. They were probably withdrawing as the troops, the army were withdrawing after this disintegration. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But during this time, you did see military vehicles on the road outside -- the road beside Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not right by the road, so I could not see exactly what was passing down the road. We would hear something. Sometimes if a person is by the road, he can see what is passing along, but not from far away.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And then one final passage from what Mr. Deronjic said. Quote: "There's an atmosphere of intimidation and killing, so they" - that's the Muslims in this period in Bratunac and Srebrenica Municipalities - "were leaving in that atmosphere. So even if it was something not directly aggressive, it was happening in this, this atmosphere that was conducive to them leaving. "The second part, the other part or number of Muslims who were not leaving because of this were to be expelled by force from the municipalities, and the part or the number of Muslims who were willing to put up resistance - so I'm talking about a third group - were the ones we were going to wage war with." My question is, were you not aware of this atmosphere of intimidation and killing of Muslims in your very municipality?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You weren't aware that Muslims were being expelled from Glogova, Suha, Zaluzje, Voljevica, or any of those places?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I was not aware of that. I did not know about that. I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Let's go briefly back to Glogova. I'm going to put to you what this Tribunal found in the Deronjic sentencing judgement the 30th of March 2004, and see if you agree that this happened. Deronjic pleaded guilty to crimes against humanity, "committed through the following underlying acts: Ordering to attack the village of Glogova on 9 May 1992; burning it down in part, and forcibly displacing of Bosnian Muslim residents from the village. As a result 64 Muslim civilians from the village were killed, Bosnian Muslim homes, private property, and a mosque were destroyed, and substantial part of Glogova was razed to the ground." That's in the sentencing judgement. In other words, across the road from you, are you saying that in May, you didn't see houses burning or hear gunshots or any of this going on? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Glogova is pretty far away from us. It's not just across the road, you see. It's several kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I won't pursue that. It's right, isn't it, that the Kravica TO was involved in the operations in Glogova? The Territorial Defence from your local community. I'm not sure if that was translated, but I think he said I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't hear the witness saying anything either.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, could the witness repeat his answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. Do you understand what I'm saying? I wasn't there, and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's because, as you were telling us, you weren't in any detachment in 1992.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I would like to put forward a Defence exhibit. It was provisionally D7 -- sorry, D6. D6. Apologies if it causes inconvenience. We can take our time.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will be given the Exhibit Number D1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does this create confusion in your ranks, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: To be D1, no, Your Honour. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's all right. So this will be D1.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If that can be placed on the ELMO. Do we have that on the ELMO? Right. We have an English translation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This is the list of conscripts of the Jezestica 1 company, and that's you at number 31, isn't it? Dragan Djuric.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
