utterances.text: I see that it says Dragan Djuric here, yes. But there are three or four Dragan Djuric that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All from Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: From the surrounding villages, yes. There are two or three in Jezestica. Two at the moment. Others moved out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If we could look at another exhibit, it will be D2.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There, again, it's headed "Jezestica 1." That would be the Ceta Jezestica 1. 33, if we can zoom out a bit. We see Dragan Djuric, Cedo, and that means Dragan Djuric whose father is Cedo. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's you, isn't it? You're not going to tell us that the other Dragan Djurics also have a father named Cedo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Not all the fathers' names are the same, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So that's you, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I am Dragan Djuric, father's name Cedo, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This document shows that you were in Jezestica Ceta 1, isn't it, in a detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know what they called it, you see. I can see here the names of almost all the people. They're older and younger. I see them all registered on this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Let's go back to D1. On the top of that, it says "spisak Vojnih Obreznika Cete Jezestica 1," "List of conscripts of the Jezestica 1 company." It's a military unit, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, do we have a date for these two documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, the date is proved by reference to the documents I'm going to introduce in a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We'll wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So, do accept that you were in a detachment, Jezestica 1?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, I don't know what they called it. I was in my village. You see what I'm saying? Now, is this a company? Is it the people of this village? Is it the local population of that village? I don't know what you're going to call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm not calling it anything, Mr. Djuric. It's headed "Ceta Jezestica 1," and it says vojnih, which means in your language "soldiers." The fact is you were not telling the truth a moment ago, were you, when you said you were not in the detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I know that I was at my home. There was no company there. There was no command there whatever. I was at home. I didn't do anything else. I was in my village, and I was at my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We have another Defence Exhibit, then, D3, which is the salaries received by persons in that detachment from July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: On the cover, we see - it's in Cyrillic - but that's July 1992, isn't it, Mr. Djuric? It's the salary lists from July 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Something like that is written on these papers here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You can read, can't you, Mr. Djuric? You're literate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, I went to school, elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You can read that? Just to establish that you're able to read. July 1992.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page of that document. Your name appears on 2130, Dragan Djuric, and there's a salary there of 9.300. I suppose it's dinars. Would that be right? It's what you received in August. Sorry, my apologies. July. If we scan to the right of that document, further, please, you see signatures. You've signed for your salary. It's right, isn't it, that you were being paid throughout this period as a member of the Jezestica 1 Ceta?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I would like the counsel to ask a question, not testify on his own behalf. To ask him did he sign -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you sign?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't see it really well here. I cannot see it here. I don't know. Perhaps there is a signature. Perhaps it has been signed. Perhaps somebody else signed. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have the original of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This document I believe is from the Bratunac collection which is in the Office of the Prosecutor's possession. But we have other documents we can come to on that subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can also put it on the ELMO for the time being, and we can have an enlargement of the signature part so that he can see better. And he has also not answered directly as well as yet the question on whether he accepts that he received a payment of 9.300 dinars at the end, or roughly towards the end, or near the end of July of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, could you please answer that question. Did you receive a salary at the end of July 1992 being in the Jezestica Ceta?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. Perhaps I did receive it. I don't remember. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So it's possible that you were paid for being a member of that detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I was in my village. If all the people who are on this list here received it, then I probably received it as well. But I really don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: People don't receive money for nothing, Mr. Djuric. If you received 9.300 dinars, what did you receive them for? For being at home and staying at home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. I'm telling you, I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You can also see on that document, can you, the words, if we can see it on the ELMO, "vod" and to the left, if you can move it slightly to the left, a bit more, there we go, stop there. That's the commander of this squadron or part of it, isn't it? Let me put it a different way. Wasn't Milosav Djukanovic the commander, as well as Bosko Rankovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I honestly think you are -- this is not contributing towards clearing up matters, Mr. Jones, because if you see Document D2 that you tendered before, the commander is shown as Nikolic, Dragan, while here it seems to be someone else. So I would stick to what is relevant as regards this witness and proceed with your questions in whichever manner is convenient for you. And then let us decide whether we believe what he is saying or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honour. There may be a distinction there's a command Cete on D1 and command Od. So it's something we can deal with later.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So we have Jezestica 1 in which you were. How many more Jezestica companies were there, if you know? I mean, if there's 1, presumably there's a 2 or a 3.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I think it refers to Jezestica as the entire village. That's what I think. But I don't know in which way that was separated and divided up.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Isn't it right that as you said your village is divided into part on the hills and a part in the valley, that Jezestica 1 was on the hills and Jezestica 2 was in the valley part?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: That's the location of our village. That's where it is. Everybody would go to the valley. That's where they build their houses so as not to be in the hills because of their children, to be closer to the road. That's where people gravitating towards.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You haven't answered my question, I'm afraid. My question is isn't one of those military detachments deployed on the hills of your village, Djermani, and the other detachment, Jezestica 2, in the valley, so that we have two military detachments in Jezestica during the war?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Witness, could you repeat your answer. Try to speak into the microphone as much as you can because sometimes the interpreters are not hearing what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how they divided it. I don't remember that, whether they divided it into Jezestica 1 and Jezestica 2. Do you know what I'm saying? I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, moving to a slightly different area, you've told us that 30 per cent of the people -- well, actually that's not -- I'm not going to be that exact this morning. You told us a number of the people from your village left at the start of the war, I believe. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Approximately how many people left your village at the start of the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I didn't count them, to be in a position to know exactly how many. A lot of people left the village, a lot of people had to leave the village. Perhaps 30 per cent or -- I don't know exactly how many. Anyone who had some family or friends somewhere, to be able to go to them, left.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And they left because there was a war going on, didn't they? That's why they left?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: That's the reason why, probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The people who left were mostly women and children, civilians.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were also people who had to leave. There were people who had to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So for the most part, there was only people mobilised into the army who remained in your village during the war? That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. There were people, there were women, there were children. It's not true that only those who were mobilised stayed behind. There were women, there were elderly women, there were other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But mostly, most of the people who remained were mobilised into the army, weren't they? The Bosnian Serb Army.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Probably if that's what they called them, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your house in Djermani, you told us, was towards Muslim villages. During the war, your village was actually on the front lines, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: There were -- there was a house in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My question was, in your village you were right on the front lines against the Muslims, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: My village, and then the next village was a Muslim village. And there was about 2 kilometres between the two villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you had trenches and minefields and all the things which go with front lines near your village, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You don't know exactly, but you are aware, aren't you, that there were minefields around your home? That's something important which you would have known about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: There were none around my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you now, with the map which is in front of you, if you could draw where the lines went during -- or just before the attack on your village on the 8th of August. Just take a pen and show us where the lines were between the Serb forces and the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If he knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: With the understanding that this piece of paper now will become an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it's not going to become an exhibit because he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Could you now give us an estimate of how many people in your village - I'm including the hamlets - were in the Territorial Defence on the 8th of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You can give us an estimate, surely.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps there were about a hundred people, maybe there were more. I don't know how many inhabitants there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Not inhabitants. How many soldiers, how many Serbs serving in the Territorial Defence or the VRS? We've seen in Jezestica 1 that there were --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I really don't know anything about that. I mean, if you have the papers, then you can look at it there. But I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You're not willing to give us an estimate, are you, because you know that there were hundreds of people, in this area in the Kravica community, who were serving in the Territorial Defence and in the Bosnian Serb Army? That's the reason, isn't it, why you're not giving us an estimate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I'm not knowledgeable about that. So I don't know. How could I tell you something that I'm not knowledgeable about and that I don't know?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Because you were serving in a Cete, in a detachment, with 40-odd people. Presumably you would know about the command structure and some of the other units with whom you were fighting alongside.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The fact is, isn't it, that everything -- every Serb in Bratunac Municipality was mobilised at the start of the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know that either. Probably that is so. Someone was forcing someone, but I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You're saying it's probably right that all Serbs in Bratunac Municipality were mobilised to fight in the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I have another exhibit, which will be D4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before we give it a number, Ms. Sellers or your case manager, are we sure that this is not also a Prosecution exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll have to check the ERN numbers to confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. But please check. In the meantime, this would be given D4, no? D4. But if it is also a Prosecution document, we need to register that. Go ahead, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you have a look at that document, Mr. Djuric. That's an order for a general mobilisation, the Serbian Municipality of Bratunac. And it appears to be mobilising citizens -- all citizens who have come of age. Now, seeing that, does that help you with the question of whether everyone was mobilised?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, were you mobilised, or did you volunteer to be in the Jezestica detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: According to these papers, I did not report anywhere, I did not go anywhere. I don't know what it states in these papers. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. My question was, when you joined Jezestica 1 Ceta, did you volunteer, or were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: If we joined, then we were mobilised. There can be nothing else. If we joined, as it states in these papers, then we were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are you only willing to admit anything which is in the papers, Mr. Djuric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: And I know that when I came, when I was wounded, when I came to look for my -- when I came back, then I was chased away by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We have a couple more Defence exhibits just dealing with the units in this area. The first one will be D5. For us it was provisionally marked D11. We may as well do three at once. Then there was D12 and D13, so that will be D5, D6, and D7. Just do them one at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The first one which you're looking at should be the list of the people in the Territorial Defence in Donji Magasici, which is near your village. You are no doubt familiar with many of the names there. Could it be that there were as many as 48 soldiers in the Donji Magasici Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not familiar with that. 7

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Then we have another -- the next exhibit, which is -- it was D12. It will be D6.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Here we have the Territorial Defence conscripts in Jezestica, August 1992. Again, I would ask you: Is that you, number 4, Dragan Djuric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know if this is my name or somebody else's name. It does say "Dragan Djuric."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We have the first vod, second vod, and then Kajici on the next page. I think you told us that Kajici is part of Jezestica. Then we have another 21 people. Would that be right, that there were as many as 21 soldiers just in Kajici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. And we see some of the other places which we referred to earlier in your testimony, Brane; Mandici, 58 soldiers; Popovici; Ocenovici. These are all in Kravica community, aren't they? There are tens if not hundreds of soldiers in your community. Are you saying that's something which you were not aware of when your village was attacked in August 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know who was where. I don't know which soldiers were stationed where. It's something that I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking you whether you knew where everyone was stationed. What I'm asking you comes down to this: You're surely aware when your village was attacked in August 1992 that there weren't 10 or 20 soldiers in the area, but hundreds of persons mobilised into the Bosnian Serb Army and the Territorial Defence who were fighting in that area? That's surely something which didn't escape your notice.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your answer because the interpreters didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said I did not hear that very well. I didn't understand the question properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Mr. Jones, could I kindly ask you to repeat it, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Perhaps I might rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There was a massive Bosnian Serb military presence in this area at this time, was there not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: In our village at the time, there was not. During the attack. Perhaps after the attack, this was true. But as far as I know, there was no such presence in our village when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Before August 1992, there were nonstop battles, were there not, between people from Jezestica and people from Glogova, elsewhere, who had taken refuge in Bijeceva and Pale and in the woods? There was nonstop conflict before that, wasn't there, before the 8th of August?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know when this happened. I don't know what date this was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You don't know the date, but you're aware that that was happening? People from Glogova were in constant struggle with the people from Jezestica and Kravica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It did happen. Not from Jezestica. I didn't go anywhere from Jezestica, and I had no business being in Glogova. I don't know about other places, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You agree that the people from Kravica were continually attacking or fighting with the Muslims from Glogova right there in your area at this time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The next Defence exhibit, which was D13 which will be D7. Your Honour, this morning when I was going through, obviously rather painfully for you, the list of hamlets and villages, it was because those appear in this list, if that wasn't clear at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: These lists show, do they not, all the units and soldiers who were in all the places in the Kravica community that you mentioned earlier, Kravica; Donji Bacici, there was an artillery group; Mandici; Brezanci; Dolovi. I've made an approximate calculation that there must have been some 600 soldiers in the Kravica community. Now, is it really your evidence there's nothing more than a few Territorial Defence soldiers defending your area? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I'm not aware of that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We'll move to a new topic. You mentioned earlier, I think, that you went to school --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you are moving into something else, we stop now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's up to you. If you have got a short series of questions, yes, we can go ahead. But it's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll be another 15 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, we need to have a break. So do I take it there is no opposition on the part of the Prosecution for these Defence exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The Prosecution will briefly allow him to continue, we'll just take note of how we will proceed in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll have a break of 25 minutes. Basically, that means we'll resume at 5 minutes to 1.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, I'm moving now to the events of 8th August 1992, the action in your village. Now, you told us that that started at 11.30 a.m. roughly. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It's around that time. I did not have a watch on my hand, but around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Around the middle of the day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You also told us, I think, that it was a surprise attack? That there was nothing -- you had nothing before then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: That's the way I remember it. For example, I know that in my village, a man was wounded before this attack. He was working in the field, and he was wounded. That's the thing I remember. Jovo Mladenovic, the late Jovo Mladenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. It's right, isn't it, that there was shooting going on all morning and this wasn't the first sounds of attack which you heard that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no shooting that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's a strange time for a surprise attack, isn't it, in the middle of the day when everyone's going about their business? Aren't surprise attacks normally at dawn?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeated his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Please repeat your answer and speak up.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I know that it was at that time. But when attacks actually take place, generally speaking, I don't know. I know when our village was attacked on the 8th of August: around 11.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you, to make myself clear, was that in fact before 11.30 when your village came under attack, there was, in fact, intensive fighting, shooting, shelling in the whole area and that's something you would have heard. And my question to you is, isn't that something that was happening on that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't think there was anything before that on that day, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that there was fierce resistance in your village from your soldiers against the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't understand that either. I know that there was no resistance. I wasn't putting up any resistance or anything. I don't know about the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, you told us that the attack lasted about two hours. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, the village was burned down, and people were killed within those two hours, in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your evidence was that the attack lasted two hours. That's right. My question is why would it take two hours if there was no resistance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Shooting was heard for about two hours. Can you understand that? The shooting around the village. Perhaps an hour and a half or two. That's as long as the shooting went on, shooting at people, the houses, the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The fact is, isn't it, that you fled at the beginning, so you weren't there and you didn't see what was going on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I've already said that. I saw people approaching houses, setting them on fire. So I had to leave my house and seek shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, is that right? Are you saying now that you saw -- saw people with your own eyes setting fire to houses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: People walked up to houses, and smoke could be seen from the houses. That meant that they were torching the houses and the houses were on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you recall making a statement in 2001 about these events, in Milici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, I do recall that I gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When you gave that statement, you were told, were you not, that you were requested to make a truthful statement of what you personally eyewitnessed? You signed that statement with a declaration that it was true to the best of your knowledge and recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could be shown a copy of his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The statement that the -- Mr. Jones is referring to, I have got the English copy of it. It's 02062554. But I can't give you the corresponding ERN number for the Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps we can approach it this way. I won't put the statement before the witness. I'll read something which is in my copy and see if he agrees with the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, put it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I put it to you that in that statement you said firstly "I wasn't aware who had been killed or what houses had been set on fire until the Muslims withdraw from the village," firstly. Secondly, you said: "I'm unable to say who attacked the village as I did not witness any of the attackers." That's what you said, is it not, when you were asked about these events in 2001? You didn't witness the attackers; you were told afterwards.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, you know what, I know about this. I was there. Now, I don't know whether these two match, you see. I mean, I was in my village. I mean, I saw houses on fire. I saw people fleeing from houses, leaving their houses as I had to.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I see these people --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you see these people, or were you told afterwards by these women who you referred to earlier? Were you told by them about what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I saw men, and I saw women, the women that are mentioned here, the two women.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I won't pursue that. You mentioned that there was shelling, shells landing, in the village. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. This house next to ours was hit by some kind of device, so the electric cable was hit. It was hit by some kind of device. Was this a shell or whatever, something fell there and exploded and hit the house therefore.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This was at the same time that you say the attackers, the locals from your neighbouring villages, were moving among the houses and doing what you say you saw them doing. It was at the same time? Muslim locals in your village moving among the houses, and a shell landing at the same time. Is that what you saw?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, no. This was at the beginning. First this house of ours was targeted, and that's when I heard the detonation. And then the shooting started -- coming from these weapons, I mean. So it was the house that was targeted first. My house, I mean, where we were. It fell by the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your evidence was that there were soldiers who attacked your village in a surprise attack. And if it was a surprise attack by soldiers, then surely a detonation couldn't have happened first.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, there were detonations, and then some kind of soldiers going from house to house and killing people. Nine people were killed in my village from my neighbourhood, members of my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If you would answer the questions which I'm asking and not volunteer answers on subjects which haven't been touched upon. Now, my suggestion to you is that shells which fell on your village were not fired by Muslims, but were part of a Serb counterattack. Do you follow that? That is my suggestion, and is it something which you would agree with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: That's not correct. These were projectiles that were fired from the woods at our village. That's where they were stationed. That's where they came to. And they approached from several different sides. They came there, and that's what they did, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: As far as you know. And you told us this morning, did you not, that you fled your village, fled for your life, in the first moments of the attack. And now you're telling us that you were able to see exactly where a projectile came from. That's surely entirely contradictory, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, this was during the first moments, these projectiles. And then I had to leave the house. Of course, when a person is afraid, he has to leave his house. And if I was not hit the first time, I could have been hit the second time, so then I had to leave my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Exactly. So you fled rapidly from the scene, and therefore didn't have much of an opportunity to see any of what passed after you fled. It has to be right, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, I went through the village. So there were different directions involved, and all of this could be seen. Some things could be seen. My house, when I got about two or three hundred metres away, I saw that it was set on fire. And the house next to my house was also on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You didn't see who did it because you didn't see the attackers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We saw people coming from those sides where there were none of our people. They were walking up to houses, shooting at the houses in the village, shooting at people from the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you saw this all as you were running away from the village; over your shoulder, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, a person has to seek shelter, go through the village. You had to go through the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You said in your earlier statement today it was only when you returned you actually saw the damage which had been done to the houses; you didn't see it at the time.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, I could not see at that moment, as I was leaving the house, I mean, as I was fleeing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Precisely. Precisely, Mr. Djuric. Now, the houses which you came back and which had been damaged by fire were mostly wooden houses in that part of the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, they were made of hard material, too, in my village. It depended on each person's possibilities and what they could afford.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's a feature of the houses in Jezestica, isn't it, that the ones on the hill are mostly made of wood?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. It was easier to use that kind of material when there were no roads. But once the roads came there, then it became easier to build houses out of hard materials like concrete blocks and bricks and other construction materials, depending on what people liked and what people could afford. But it depended on whether the material used was the older type or the more recent type for building roofs and for beams and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll read you what you said in your prior statement. You said: "In the village, 60 houses were set on fire. A significant part of those houses were made out of wood, so it was very easy to start a fire internally in the house. The houses were ablaze for a period of four or five house. Nobody could deter the progress or the rapid burn of the houses." Now, you know this village very well, Mr. Djuric. Do you want to give us an honest answer as to whether those houses were of wood or whether they weren't? Were you lying in your 2003 statement, 2001, or are you lying now?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask Counsel to please let the witness answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Sellers is right. Mr. Djuric, could you please give us an answer. Which version is the correct one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, it all depended on one's possibilities, on what a person could afford. The older houses were not built of wood only. Still they used bricks, and then these beams were made, and -- these were the old-type houses. But then there were new-type houses where concrete slabs were used and bricks and so on. So there were both types of houses. And people lived in these houses, and they had nowhere else to live.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, you have not answered the question. The question that was put to you is a very simple one, sir. It was put to you that when you were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecution way back in I think December of 2003 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 2001, yeah. No, the date of the interview is 11 December 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was referring to the other one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have it even here. Paragraph 12 of that statement reads: "In the village, 60 houses were set on fire. I know the families and can name the owners of those homes. The significant part of those houses was made out of wood, so it was very easily to start a fire internally in the house. The houses were ablaze for a period of four to five hours." And then in the second statement, you say more or less the same thing, unless it was copied: "In the village, 60 houses were set on fire. I know the families and name the owners of those homes. The significant part of those houses was made of wood, so it was very easy -- easily," again, it is said there, "to start a fire internally in the house." So the question is when you stated to the officer from the Office of the Prosecution that the significant part of those 60 houses were set on fire were made of wood, were you saying something correct or something which now you say is not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you know what? I don't know how they understood this. Well, made of wood. Sir, I don't know whether you had the opportunity of seeing this. The ground floor was made of stone, and then after that, bricks were used. And then wooden beams, and then there was mortar, and this is what our houses look like. But then there were these newer houses, too, you see, made of these other materials, sand, concrete blocks, et cetera. I know what my house was like, too. And then we adjust -- then we made some adjustments and we did some additional construction.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I won't stop you pursuing this if you want to, but it's up to you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just a question about the extent of the damage. When you returned and saw the damage to the village, you said you still had a cellar, so your house obviously wasn't completely destroyed. Is it your evidence that all 60 houses were completely destroyed or that some were partially damaged to different degrees? What precisely are you able to tell us on that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, it all depended on the house involved, what material was made of. My house was on fire then at that moment. The upper storey was burning, and attic was burning and --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll put it much more simply. 60 houses, obviously they weren't destroyed all to the same extent, were they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: In these few hamlets, there were about 60 houses. I can give you the names of the owners of these houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The question is simply this: The ones that were damaged were damaged to different extents, weren't they? You mentioned your roof had caught fire; maybe others suffered more or less damage. My question is wasn't there different degrees of damage to the different houses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, different, yes. It's not that a slab of concrete can burn the way a wooden beam can burn or a wooden post. But it is true that people could not go on living in houses like that. The people who lived in these houses before.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I want to ask you about the objects which were -- went missing from your village after the attack. You said that you lost your cows, but that you got your pigs back. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: As far as the cows are concerned, you have no idea, do you, whether they were actually stolen or whether they got free during the attack and went off on their own?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I know that they weren't where they had been left.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, after the 8th of August 1992, did you stay in the army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I stayed in my village, in that village. I'm telling you that. The place where my wife's house is, the house that had not burned down. That's what I was telling you. That's where I stayed, in her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My question is did you remain a soldier after the 8th of August attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: How can a person say that? If somebody is a soldier, then he's a soldier, whereas I stayed in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We have another Defence exhibit. It will be D8. It was 14 on our list.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This is dated November 1992. I'll ask you to turn to the third page in the Serbian version. There we see number 295, Djuric, Cedo, son of Cedo. My apologies, yes, Dragan. And this is, is it not, the 3rd Infantry unit, Bratunac Brigade? You find your name there, and your father's name, 295 on the third page. We can see this is November 1992, after the events in your village. 295. I don't know if you see it. Djuric, Cedo, Dragan.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact, you were in the 3rd Infantry Unit at this time in the Bratunac Brigade, weren't you? It's something you would know about, wouldn't you, if you were in that unit, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know what they call them. Do you see what I'm saying about these lists? Do you understand what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I understand that you're denying that you were in the army, and there's a piece of paper in front of you which makes it very clear that you were in the 3rd Infantry Unit. If that's your position, that you weren't --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: If that's what the papers say, then we were. I was in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, are you able to give an honest answer without having a piece of paper put in front of you to show the truth? You're here to tell the truth irrespective of whether we can prove it with a piece of paper. My question to you is: Were you or were you not in the 3rd Infantry Unit in the Bratunac Brigade in November 1992? Paid for being so, paid for official trips?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that. What they called us, what unit and how they called us, the name, I mean. I was in my village, and I'm not aware of any trips or paying for some trips. I don't know anything about that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It doesn't matter what they called your unit. The point is that you were in the Bratunac Brigade in November 1992, and you have been denying it today in court. But I won't pursue it. If we can move on to one further point: How long did you actually remain in the Bosnian Serb Army?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My apologies. Perhaps we need to give the exhibit a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Can you tell us honestly how long you remained in the Bosnian Serb Army and the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't quite understand this. What do you mean how long? I mean, I was not there. You mean when I came back, I had to be there again? I mean, the police?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll put it very simply for you. Were you in the Bratunac Brigade right up until 1995? July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: In Bratunac, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Ah, the Bratunac Brigade, well...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The previous document we saw, it referred to the fact that you were in the 3rd Infantry Company. Surely you're not telling us you don't know what the 1st Infantry Company was, the 2nd Company, what brigade you were in. Surely you were aware you were in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, we knew that we were in Bratunac, but I don't know about these companies or brigades. You see what I'm saying? I don't know what they call this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: A final Defence exhibit, which is -- one more Defence exhibit which is -- it will be D9. This is from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You can see the date, 02 1995 in the original version, and then February 1995 in the English. If you turn to page 2, number 137, Djuric, Cedo, Dragan, 2nd Infantry Detachment, you've even signed there, haven't you? I think it's right to say that your signature is easily matched with that on your witness statement. In any event, you signed, did you not? February 1995 as a member of the 2nd Infantry Detachment, Bratunac Brigade, that's you, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You are going to completely deny that you were ever a soldier, Mr. Djuric? I'll remind you that you are under oath, and there are penalties for false testimony at this Tribunal. Were you or were you not a soldier in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, if the name is there, I had to be there. I was forced to be there, if that's the Bratunac Brigade. You understand? I came there when I was wounded under pressure. They made me go.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think finally you've admitted it. You were in the Bratunac Brigade. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade, so we were there, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just a few questions now on Kravica and the events of the 7th of January 1993. It's right to say, isn't it, that at that time, several months after the attack on your village, Kravica was a major Bosnian Serb military stronghold attacking towards Glogova in the period running up to 7th of January. I put it to you that that's something which was the case and you knew about it as a member of the military.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: As far as that was concerned, I didn't know anything. I was in my village. But I didn't have any links with anybody to know anything more or in more depth about anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You mentioned that this was Christmas for Orthodox Christians. It's right, isn't it, that you traditionally celebrate that by having very large feasts, lots of food, cakes, meats, and that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was a custom. I was at home by myself. I didn't have any reason to celebrate anything. My wife wasn't there. My child wasn't there. The same thing applied to all of my neighbours, that there was not really that much to celebrate.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My point is that on this day, 7th of January 1993, the Serbs in the Kravica community were preparing feasts, preparing a very large quantity of food to have that day, weren't they, as is their custom? You can answer that with a simple yes, no, or I don't know.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: You know how it is. I know that in every household, that day was marked. Those who had something to make, bake or roast, they would do that. Guests would not be going anywhere as --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]....

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: -- it would not be some -- those who could, they could go. I mean, it could be like a sort of celebratory lunch or dinner in somebody's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking that question, Mr. Djuric, is that it's right, isn't it, that at that time the Serbs in Jezestica and Kravica eat a large amount of food at the time when the Muslims nearby whom you mentioned shooting at you in the forests were starving. I put it to you that that was something you knew at the time.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know who had what quantities of food. I know about my own house, for example, but I don't know about the other people, what they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You are not aware that throughout this whole period the people from Glogova and elsewhere were trying to get food because they didn't have any, because they were cut off from food. That's something you say you don't know about? If you don't know, you don't know.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: That people didn't have any food.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Let's turn to Kravica now on the 7th of January. You've referred to men in white who you saw among the houses. You mentioned that you saw smoke. On that occasion, you didn't actually make an assessment of the amount of damage which was done, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. I only saw that in my own village. I couldn't see that in Kravica. The people in white and the smoke was in my village before I went to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You mentioned that the men in white who you saw in Kravica also shot at you, shot at you from the hills, and that these were local -- locals from neighbouring Muslim villages. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: This was in Jezestica, not in Kravica, as far as I remember. It was in Jezestica, in my village, and not in Kravica as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: They were locals from neighbouring villages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They were our neighbours from neighbouring villages, Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you also see a very large number of civilians moving among the men who you've described as being in white?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I did not notice that. At the point in time when I was leaving my village and when I was wounded, all I saw were these men in white. I didn't see if there were any other people amongst them, and I wasn't able to see who was coming in from each side, because, like I said, they were coming or approaching the village from different sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You didn't see thousands of civilians, men, women, children, women in demija, as I believe they're called, moving among the soldiers or the men in white among the houses? That's something you say you didn't see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I was not in a position to see something like that with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you told us how you were wounded. Are you telling us that you were a civilian on that occasion when you were wounded? You weren't actually in combat?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I was withdrawing from my own village. I was going towards Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I have one more Defence exhibit, which will be D9. Sorry, D10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: D10 it will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I will ask you just to look on the first page. And we have a translation: "List of wounded, 7 January 1993." If we look down to number 14, it has been crossed out and says 11, "Dragan, son of Cedo, Djuric. Born 1963, 3rd Infantry Batallion, wounded in Kajici." This shows, does it not, that when you were wounded you were wounded as a soldier serving in the 3rd Infantry Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: If it was the military, then that's a soldier, you understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You had a weapon with you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just wonder why have you been beating around the bush trying to evade answering questions that are related or trying to prove that you were a member of the armed forces of Republika Srpska or the Bosnian Serb Army? What are you afraid of? Other Serbs who were in that army are probably proud to have been in that army. Why are you so reticent? Why are you not even trying to admit that you were part of that army? What are you ashamed of or afraid of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you know how it is. We were in our village. I don't know. If it was the Serbian Army or the Army of the Republika Srpska, then that's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there re-examination, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, there isn't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have any questions? Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Well, I would like the witness to tell me what kind of weapon did you have in your -- you personally -- have in your possession in your village? You told me that some of the villagers had hunting rifles and some had pistols, as far as I remember. What did you have.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I didn't have any weapons at that time. Some weapons were being given out, but I don't know, you understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: No, I don't quite. What do you mean by "weapons were given out"? Does that mean that every male member of this small village, society, did have weapons given to them? What do you mean by "given out"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, could you answer the -- repeat your answer, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: As far as I recall, if some people had weapons or if they did not have weapons, well, I cannot recall everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: When you were a member, as tested here, or registered as a member of this group, armed group, were you given any uniform of any kind?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: There was no uniform. Perhaps some people had uniforms. But later, they received uniforms. At the beginning, there were no uniforms. I personally at that time didn't have a uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: When did you get a uniform, then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We only got them later when I -- I personally got one when I came and when I was picked up again in 1993, sometime in October. Perhaps it was at that time. Maybe it was a little later. I don't remember. As far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: This unit in the village, we have seen all the names you say, a great number of names of male inhabitants in your village, did you have any kind of training together during that period? That means from July, August, and up to January 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJURIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I did not go to any training then. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I have a question to the Prosecution with regard to the issue of hearsay evidence. We have heard from the witness that he spoke to Stanica and Perka Djuric. Another question is have these two persons he was reporting on also been questioned by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, they have not been questioned by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And why not, if they would have been able to give direct evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm unaware of that. I will check and get back to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That brings your testimony to an end, Mr. Djuric. I thank you for having come over to give evidence, and I hope we will not need to see you again. You will now be escorted by the usher. And should you need any assistance to enable you to return to your country, I'm sure that you will find it available. Have a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may be allowed to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because -- well, I just want to say that in my village, nine people were killed on the 8th of August, nine people, including men and women. There were also people who were wounded. And on the 7th of January, 18 people were killed on the 7th of January from my village. These were people who were killed in my village. And I can give you their names. For example, for the 8th of August and for the 7th of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have their names already. We have their names. Do you have anything else to state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Usher, please could you escort the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I suppose we meet again tomorrow morning at 9.00 with the same witness -- try to -- not the same -- with another witness. It's going to haunt me between now and tomorrow. We'll have the next witness. And try, please, to make sure that if you are going to make use of particular documents that you already have in mind, to make the Prosecution aware of that so they will be prepared. Same applies to you. Please let us know beforehand what documents you may - because this is always may - use in the course of your testimony. All right. Thank you. Again once more, I wish to thank everyone because we have gone beyond our time again. Thanks. And we'll meet tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 15th day of October, at, 2004 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
